mainTopic: Which kinds of contact by a גוי make Jewish wine forbidden: a split barrel, a winepress, and the משנה's cases of a loan, indirect contact, and a barrel thrown in anger.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a barrel that split while a גוי hugged it closed. If it split lengthwise, the wine may only be sold to גוים. If it split widthwise, even drinking is allowed, because he was just acting like a brick. רב אשי then explains how to clean a winepress a גוי stood in. A new משנה follows with several cases. A גוי found by the vat forbids the wine only if the owner owes him money. When a גוי fell in or touched the wine indirectly, the חכמים say it may be sold and רבי שמעון permits it. A barrel thrown in anger was declared fit. In the גמרא, שמואל limits the loan case to a loan tied to that wine, and רב אשי proves this from the בית שאן משנה. רב פפא adds that a גוי who came out of the vat alive forbids the wine, because he treats his rescue like a holiday. The גמרא praises רבי שמעון's all-or-nothing view but rules against him. Finally, רב אשי compares a גוי's contact to a זב's, and רב הונא challenges this comparison from the words "in his anger."

steps.title: A gentile hugs a barrel that split lengthwise
steps.stepSummary: A barrel split lengthwise and a גוי grabbed it. רפרם בר פפא (or רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) allowed the wine to be sold to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A barrel split from top to bottom, and a non-Jew jumped up and wrapped his arms around it. רפרם בר פפא, or some say רב הונא son of רב יהושע, allowed the wine to be sold to non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began before this section: a barrel split, a גוי hugged it closed, and a חכם ruled the wine could be sold to גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Allowing a sale to גוים means the wine was forbidden for drinking but not forbidden for all benefit. The גוי's grabbing counts as real contact with the wine, but not the kind that makes it totally forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: he hugged it / wrapped his arms around it

phrases.english: that split lengthwise,
phrases.notes: We're joining a story partway through; "that" is a barrel of wine.

phrases.english: a certain gentile jumped up and hugged it,
Rafram bar Pappa permitted it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
to sell to gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a case story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine in a lengthwise-split barrel that a גוי hugged closed may be sold to גוים, but not drunk.

steps.title: Limiting the ruling to a lengthwise split
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies only to a lengthwise split. If the barrel split widthwise, even drinking the wine is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only applies when it split lengthwise. But if it split widthwise, it is permitted even for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the last ruling. It splits the case into two kinds of cracks with different outcomes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a lengthwise crack, the גוי pulls the two separating halves together, which רש״י explains counts as touching the wine through the halves of the barrel (though without stirring), so the wine is forbidden for drinking. In a widthwise crack, he only holds the top and bottom halves together, and the wine becomes fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: and these words apply (only)… — a limiting phrase

phrases.english: And this applies only where it split lengthwise,
but if it split widthwise —
it is permitted even for drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of step 1 and adds a more lenient case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lengthwise split: may only be sold. Widthwise split: even drinking is permitted.

steps.title: Why is the widthwise case fully permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the full leniency in the widthwise case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wine is allowed even for drinking when the barrel split widthwise. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. It asks for the logic that separates the widthwise case from the lengthwise case.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 2's widthwise leniency.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a גוי holding a widthwise-split barrel does not forbid the wine at all.

steps.title: He is just acting like a brick
steps.stepSummary: The גוי is only doing what a brick would do. He weighs the barrel down and does nothing to the wine itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is just doing the job of a brick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: in the widthwise case, the גוי is just a weight holding the top half down on the bottom half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brick placed on the barrel would do the same job. So the גוי's action is not treated as handling the wine at all, and it is fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: the action of a brick (just a weight)

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי's touch matters only when he actually deals with the wine. Simply acting as a weight, like a brick, does not forbid it.

phrases.english: He is performing the action of a brick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גוי is just a weight holding the barrel together, so his action does not count as handling the wine.

steps.title: A gentile standing in a winepress
steps.stepSummary: A גוי was found standing in a winepress. רב אשי rules that the cleaning needed depends on how much wine is still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-Jew was found standing in a winepress. רב אשי said: if there is enough wetness to make other things wet, the press needs rinsing and also a more thorough cleaning. If not, just rinsing is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new case story: a גוי was found standing in a winepress. רב אשי explains how to clean the press afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If enough wine remains to wet something else (טופח להטפיח), the גוי's contact has a stronger effect, so the press needs both rinsing and a fuller cleaning. If the wetness is less than that, rinsing alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: wet enough to make something else wet

phrases.english: A certain gentile who was found
standing in a winepress,
Rav Ashi said:
If there is enough moisture to moisten other things —
it needs rinsing and it needs a more thorough cleaning,
and if not —
simple rinsing is enough for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גּוֹי דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח דַּהֲוָה קָאֵי בְּמַעְצַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case, separate from the split barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the press is wet enough to wet other things, it needs rinsing plus a fuller cleaning. Otherwise rinsing alone is enough.

steps.title: משנה: a gentile found next to the wine vat
steps.stepSummary: A גוי found standing next to a wine vat: if the owner owes him a loan, the wine is forbidden. If not, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A non-Jew who was found standing beside a vat of wine: if he has a loan owed to him by the owner, the wine is forbidden. If he has no loan owed to him, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a גוי found beside a wine vat, and the answer depends on whether the owner owes him money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody saw the גוי touch the wine, so the question is whether we assume he did. A גוי who is owed money feels he has a claim on the owner's property and may handle it freely. Without a loan, we assume he did not touch wine that is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: a loan owed to him (by the owner)

steps.confusionAlert: "יש לו מלוה עליו" means the owner owes the גוי money, not the other way around. That debt is what makes him feel free to handle the wine.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A gentile who was found standing
next to the wine vat,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ מִלְוָה עָלָיו — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: if he has a loan owed to him by the owner, it is forbidden,
if he has no loan owed to him, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: נׇכְרִי שֶׁנִּמְצָא עוֹמֵד בְּצַד הַבּוֹר שֶׁל יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי near the vat makes it forbidden only if the owner owes him a loan.

steps.title: משנה: indirect contacts where the wine may be sold
steps.stepSummary: A גוי fell in and climbed out, measured with a pole, flicked out a hornet with a pole, or skimmed foam off a fermenting barrel. The חכמים: sell it. רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he fell into the vat and came up, measured it with a pole, flicked a hornet out with a pole, or was skimming foam off the top of a fermenting barrel: each of these really happened, and the חכמים said it should be sold. רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists four real cases of indirect or unintended contact. The חכמים said the wine may only be sold, and רבי שמעון disagrees and permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the גוי did not handle the wine in the normal way: he fell in by accident, or touched it only through a pole or while skimming foam. The חכמים forbid drinking but allow benefit, so it may be sold. רבי שמעון holds this kind of contact does not forbid the wine at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he measured it with a pole

phrases.english: If he fell into the vat and came up,
measured it with a pole,
flicked out the hornet with a pole,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְטַפֵּיחַ עַל פִּי חָבִית מְרוּתַּחַת —
phrases.english: or was skimming foam off the top of a fermenting barrel —
in all of these there was an actual incident
and they said: it should be sold,
and Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with more cases of a גוי's contact with wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: indirect contact makes the wine forbidden to drink but allowed to sell. רבי שמעון: fully permitted.

steps.title: משנה: a barrel thrown into the vat in anger
steps.stepSummary: A גוי grabbed a barrel and threw it into the vat in anger. This really happened, and the wine was declared fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took the barrel and threw it into the vat in his anger: this really happened, and they declared it fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case where a גוי threw a barrel into the vat in a rage, and the חכמים ruled the wine fully kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more lenient than the previous step: here even drinking is allowed. The משנה just reports the ruling without giving a reason. The גמרא later builds רב אשי's general rule on this case and then challenges it.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה moves from strict to lenient. If the owner owes the גוי a loan, the wine is forbidden. Indirect contact means it may only be sold (רבי שמעון permits it). A barrel thrown in anger is fully kosher.

phrases.english: If he took the barrel
and threw it in his anger into the vat,
this was an actual incident, and they declared it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל אֶת הֶחָבִית וּזְרָקָהּ בַּחֲמָתוֹ לַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final, even more lenient case to the list in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine in a barrel a גוי threw into the vat in anger is fit, even for drinking.

steps.title: שמואל limits the loan case to a loan tied to that wine
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's loan case forbids the wine only when the גוי has a claim on that specific wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל says: This rule applies only when the גוי has a loan that is tied to that wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. שמואל adds a condition to the case of the גוי standing by the vat whose owner owes him money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the owner owes the גוי a loan, the wine is forbidden. שמואל narrows this. A general debt is not enough. The loan must be tied to this wine, so the גוי feels he has a right to it and might touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
And this is only when (a phrase that limits a rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the worry is not a debt in general. The worry is that the גוי thinks he has a right to this wine.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel says:
And this is when he has a loan
on that wine.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's case from step 6, where the wine owner owes the גוי money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִלְוָה עַל אוֹתוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the loan case from the משנה (step 6).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is forbidden only if the גוי's loan is tied to that specific wine.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the case in בית שאן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a later משנה about a Jew who made a גוי's wine kosher and left it with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording of the משנה also shows this. We learned: A Jew made a גוי's wine kosher and left it in the גוי's property. If the גוי wrote him, 'I received money from you,' the wine is permitted. But if the Jew wanted to take the wine out and the גוי would not let him until he paid, this happened in בית שאן and the חכמים forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי supports שמואל by quoting another משנה. This step quotes the source, and the next step draws the lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the גוי holds onto the wine until he is paid. So the wine itself acts as security for the money. That is exactly the kind of loan 'tied to the wine' that שמואל described.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה's wording also shows this
One who makes the wine kosher
A city in ארץ ישראל where this case happened

steps.confusionAlert: Here the wine belongs to the Jew. The גוי is only holding onto it until he is paid.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The mishna is also precise this way,
as we learned:
One who makes a gentile's wine pure
phrases.notes: A Jew prepares the גוי's wine himself so that it stays kosher and can be sold to Jews.

phrases.english: and places it in his domain,
and that one writes for him:
"I received money from you" — it is permitted,
but if the Jew wants to take it out
and he does not let him
until he gives him his money,
this was an incident in Beit She'an
and they prohibited it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support שמואל's condition.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the loan must be tied to that wine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the incident in בית שאן

steps.title: The lesson from 'he does not let him'
steps.stepSummary: The wine was forbidden only because the גוי would not release it, so a loan tied to the wine is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it was forbidden is that the גוי would not let him take the wine. But if he had let him, it would be permitted. Learn from this: we need a loan that is tied to that wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws the lesson from the משנה he just quoted. He shows that it fits שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the Jew still owes money, the wine is permitted as long as the גוי lets him take it. The wine becomes forbidden only when the גוי holds it as security. So a simple debt is not enough, and the loan has to be tied to the wine.

phrases.english: The reason is that he does not let him,
but if he lets him, it is permitted,
learn from this:
we require a loan on that wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאֵין מַנִּיחוֹ, הָא מַנִּיחוֹ שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opposite case in the בית שאן משנה: if the גוי lets him take the wine, it is permitted

steps.title: The גמרא agrees with the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof for שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn this from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the proof works. שמואל's rule is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one argues with the proof. The loan case in our משנה is settled: the wine is forbidden only when the loan is tied to that wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. Said again as an answer, it means 'yes, we learn it'

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי's loan makes the wine forbidden only if the loan is tied to that wine, so the גוי feels he has a right to it.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with the lesson drawn in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's rule stands: there must be a loan tied to that wine.

steps.title: רב פפא: only if the גוי came out dead
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the משנה's case of a גוי who fell into the vat. The lenient ruling applies only if he came out dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: He fell into the vat and came up. רב פפא says: This was taught only when he came up dead. But if he came up alive, the wine is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case from the משנה. רב פפא puts a limit on the lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 7) let the wine be sold after a גוי fell in. רב פפא says that applies only if the גוי died. If he survived, the wine is fully forbidden, even for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the vat where wine is collected

phrases.english: He fell into the vat and came up.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 7.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
They taught this only where he came up dead,
but if he came up alive — it is prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפַל לַבּוֹר וְעָלָה. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁעָלָה מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the loan case to the case of the גוי who fell in, from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גוי came out alive, the wine is forbidden, even for benefit.

steps.title: Why does it matter if he came out alive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב פפא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a living גוי makes the wine forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling in by accident does not seem like pouring wine for an idol. So why should it matter whether he lived? The גמרא wants the reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a גוי who comes out alive makes the wine forbidden.

steps.title: He treats his rescue like a holiday
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains: a גוי who was saved feels the day is like his holiday, so he may pour the wine to his idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because to him the day feels like their holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reason for his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי who was saved from death is thankful. To him the day is like a holiday for his idol. On such a day he may pour wine to the idol to give thanks, so the wine is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: If a גוי falls into the wine and comes out alive, the wine is forbidden, because he treats his rescue like a holiday for his idol.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because it seems to him
like their festival day.
phrases.notes: He is grateful he survived, so he might pour the wine to his idol to give thanks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּדָמֵי עֲלֵיהּ כְּיוֹם אֵידָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי who was rescued treats that day like a holiday for his idol and may pour the wine to it.

steps.title: The משנה's pole cases: sold, but רבי שמעון permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a גוי who touched wine with a pole. The חכמים say the wine may only be sold, and רבי שמעון permits it fully.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if a גוי measured the wine with a pole, and so on. All these cases really happened, and the חכמים said the wine should be sold. רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new piece of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the next comments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי touched the wine only through a pole, not with his hand. The חכמים take a middle position: the wine may be sold to a גוי, but a Jew may not drink it. רבי שמעון says even drinking is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It should be sold (to a גוי), but not drunk

phrases.english: He measured it with a pole, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה's list: flicking a hornet out with a pole, and skimming foam off a fermenting barrel.

phrases.english: All these were an actual incident
and they said: it should be sold,
and רבי שמעון permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה after רב פפא's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גוי touches wine with a pole, the חכמים allow selling it but not drinking it. רבי שמעון allows drinking it.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה praises רבי שמעון's consistency
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה blesses רבי שמעון because his view has no middle ground: wine is either fully permitted or fully forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: May blessings rest on רבי שמעון's head! When he permits, he permits even drinking. When he forbids, he forbids even getting any benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא praises רבי שמעון's approach to the pole case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים's ruling is in the middle: the wine may be sold, so benefit is allowed, but drinking is not. רבי שמעון has no such in-between category. If wine is really יין נסך, all benefit is forbidden. If it is not, it may even be drunk.

keyTerms.meaning: May blessings rest on his head, a phrase of praise

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: יָנוּחוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרָכוֹת עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: May blessings rest on רבי שמעון's head,
when he permits, he permits even drinking,
and when he forbids, he forbids even benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָנוּחוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרָכוֹת עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on רבי שמעון's view quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון's approach is all-or-nothing: either fully permitted, even for drinking, or fully forbidden, even for benefit.

steps.title: Traditions that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Several chains of tradition, through רב חסדא from רב or from זעירי, report that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of אבא בר נחמני said that רב חסדא said in the name of רב, and some say רב חסדא said in the name of זעירי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. Others say that רב חסדא said: אבא בר חנן told me that זעירי said this: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings reports that the הלכה is like רבי שמעון. It lists different versions of who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the versions agree on the ruling itself. They differ only on the chain of people who passed it on: רב, or זעירי directly, or זעירי through אבא בר חנן. This sets up the surprise in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּאַבָּא בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya son of Abba bar Naḥmani said,
Rav Ḥisda said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי:
phrases.english: and some say: Rav Ḥisda said that Ze'eiri said:
The halakha follows רבי שמעון.
There are those who say: Rav Ḥisda said:
Abba bar Ḥanan told me,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר זְעֵירִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: this is what Ze'eiri said: The halakha follows רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After praising רבי שמעון's logic, the גמרא reports rulings that follow him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to these traditions, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The final ruling: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Despite all the traditions, the גמרא concludes that the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final decision, and it goes against the traditions it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with the praise and the reported rulings, the final law follows the חכמים. Wine touched by a גוי with a pole may be sold but not drunk.

keyTerms.meaning: But the law is not (like this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the חכמים win: wine a גוי touched with a pole may be sold but not drunk.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop reading after "the הלכה follows רבי שמעון." The very next line reverses it, and that is the final ruling.

phrases.english: But the halakha does not follow רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the rulings reported in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the חכמים, not רבי שמעון. The wine may be sold but may not be drunk.

steps.title: The משנה's angry barrel-throwing case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a גוי who threw a barrel into the vat in anger, where the wine was ruled fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a גוי took a barrel and threw it, in his anger, into the vat. This really happened, and they ruled the wine fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. This sets up רב אשי's general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי caused the wine to reach the vat, but by throwing it in anger. He was not handling it in a normal way. The חכמים ruled the wine kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: The pit or vat where the wine collects

phrases.english: He took a barrel and threw it [in his anger] into the vat,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets, but the full wording of the משנה, quoted below, does include them.

phrases.english: this was an actual incident [and they ruled it fit].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrel a גוי threw into the vat in anger was ruled fit.

steps.title: רב אשי: a גוי's touch works like a זב's touch
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a general rule. Any contact through which a זב makes something טמא is contact through which a גוי makes wine into יין נסך, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: any way a זב makes something טמא, a גוי makes wine into יין נסך in that same way. Any way a זב leaves something טהור, a גוי does not make wine into יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a general measuring rule for what kinds of a גוי's contact make wine forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of judging each case on its own, רב אשי links two areas of law. The laws of how a זב passes on טומאה are well defined. So he uses them as the yardstick for when a גוי's contact counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a certain bodily discharge, who passes on strong טומאה
Wine forbidden because a גוי may have offered it to his idol

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives a clear standard for all the contact cases in the משנה. It is the rule רב הונא tests in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Any way in which a zav makes something impure,
in a gentile, it makes libation wine,
any way in which a zav leaves something pure,
in a gentile, it does not make libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁבַּזָּב טָמֵא בְּגוֹי עוֹשֶׂה יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general principle related to the barrel-throwing case of step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי's contact makes wine into יין נסך exactly when the same contact by a זב would pass on טומאה.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges רב אשי from the word "in his anger"
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes the משנה in full. It says the wine was permitted because the גוי threw it in anger, which implies that without anger it would be forbidden. That does not fit רב אשי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא challenged רב אשי: the משנה says a גוי took the barrel and threw it in his anger into the vat. This happened in בית שאן, and they ruled it fit. So if he threw it in anger, yes, it is permitted. But if not in anger, no, it is not permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא attacks רב אשי's rule using an exact reading of the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the זב yardstick, throwing an object would not pass on טומאה, so it should never make יין נסך. Yet the משנה needed to say "in his anger." That suggests a calm throw would forbid the wine. So the זב comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the incident happened
Yes / no, the pattern of drawing an inference from what the text implies

phrases.english: Rav Huna challenged Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל אֶת הֶחָבִית וּזְרָקָהּ בַּחֲמָתוֹ לַבּוֹר,
phrases.english: He took the barrel and threw it in his anger into the vat,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבֵית שְׁאָן וְהִכְשִׁירוּ.
phrases.english: this was an incident in Beit She'an, and they ruled it fit.
In his anger, yes;
not in his anger, no!
phrases.notes: The point: a זב throwing something wouldn't make it טמא, so by רב אשי's rule even a calm throw should be fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's rule from step 21 using the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that a גוי makes יין נסך only through contact that would make a זב's touch טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words "in his anger" imply that a calm throw would forbid the wine. But a זב's throw does not pass on טומאה, so רב אשי's rule would permit even a calm throw.
